original.target_description: Closest explicitly printed relationship on the supplied locator: Openness/complexity at age 21 predicting Identity Acceptance at age 43, Figure 3, in Mills Longitudinal Study women. This is a different identity dimension from Identity Integration; Figure 2 uses Capacity for Status to predict Identity Integration. Therefore these located values are a known outcome mismatch, not verified statistics for the requested integration/consolidation outcome.

n.sample_role: Women included in the Figure 3 mediated path models of Openness/complexity at age 21, Identity Acceptance at age 43, and Environmental Mastery or Personal Growth at age 60.
n.exclusions: Figure-specific exclusion or missing-data rules not documented here; p. 999 states that analysis-specific n varies with participation. Do not substitute the overall sample of 111.

es.location: Published p. 1003 (PDF p. 9), Figure 3, Openness/complexity Age 21 → Identity Acceptance Age 43 path, repeated in both panels. Caption identifies numbers next to arrows as standardized path coefficients.

p.location: Published p. 1003 (PDF p. 9), Figure 3, asterisk on the -.50 path and significance key at the end of the caption.

notes: Title and authors verified in the published scanned article; numerical values, labels, caption N, and significance key checked visually on PDF p. 9. Printed metric retained without conversion. Figure 3 measures identity acceptance (versus searching), whereas identity integration is explicitly distinguished as a separate dimension on pp. 998 and 1000. The located coefficient, n, and p all belong to Figure 3; they must not be treated as a match to identity integration merely because the broad locator names p. 9. No coefficient for openness predicting identity integration was established. Replication and narrative replication success are unassigned.
